sections.html:
No Ocean County town has more residents than Lakewood: 143,765 in the 2025 estimate, up from 135,158 in 2020. Subdivisions spread quickly after the 1960s. Today's parcels run from older single-family lots near the lakes to newer builds and big condominium communities, so assessments differ sharply even a few blocks apart.

A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $466,700, and median gross rent is $1,774. Owners live in 51.5 percent of homes and the rest are rented, which makes many sellers landlords with tenants in place. Expect a buyer to ask for leases, the rent roll and open repair requests. Unpaid tax on a rental carries the same lien risk as on a home the owner lives in.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in the Municipal Building
sections.html:
Two desks inside the Municipal Building at 231 Third Street, Lakewood, NJ 08701, split the work. The Tax Assessor fixes the assessed value of each parcel, while the Tax Collector mails the bill and receives payment. The county tax board in Toms River hears assessment appeals.

  • Tax Assessor: 732-364-2500, extension 5248, open 8:30 AM to 5 PM. Ownership records, name and address changes and senior, disability and veteran deduction forms go through this office.
  • Tax Collector: 732-364-2500, open 9 AM to 5 PM. Bring payment questions, payoff requests and tax sale concerns to this desk.
  • Ocean County Board of Taxation: receives appeals at the Courthouse on Washington Street in Toms River.

A new deed reaches the tax records when the Ocean County Clerk forwards it to the assessor, and the collector then works from the assessor's file. If a closing is close, ask the assessor to confirm the owner of record so the bill and any payoff request go to the right name.

sections.h2: Due dates and late payment costs
sections.html:
Four dates matter in Lakewood: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. A 10-day grace period follows each one, so money that reaches the office by the 10th owes no interest. The township counts from the day it receives payment, and a postmark does not help.

One bill arrives each summer with four coupons attached. Quarters one and two are each set from half of last year's bill. Quarters three and four use this year's rate, so they run higher after a rate increase and lower after a cut. A missing bill is no excuse, and having a lender escrow account does not shift the duty off you.

Lakewood late-payment charges
ChargeRateApplies to
Interest8% a yearFirst $1,500 of a delinquency
Interest18% a yearEvery dollar over $1,500
Year-end penalty6%Open tax and interest above $10,000 on December 31, after which the whole amount accrues at 18% from January 1

A balance counts as current once all earlier bills are paid before the next quarter comes due.

sections.h2: What a payoff looks like at a sale
sections.html:
Owing tax does not stop a Lakewood sale. The closing agent takes the open amount from the seller's proceeds and records the payment. Get a figure from the collector that runs through the closing date and includes interest earned so far.

The bigger concern is a tax sale lien. Each year the township auctions liens for the prior year's unpaid municipal charges, which covers water, sewer, maintenance liens and taxes. The auction does not hand over the house. What the winning bidder gets is a lien on the parcel, and it earns interest until you redeem it.

Lienholders usually record the lien with the Ocean County Clerk, and a recorded lien blocks clear title. Redemption has to be in full and in guaranteed funds. Foreclosure can start six months after the sale when the township holds the lien, or after two years when a third party bought it. Spot a certificate on your parcel and the collector can give you the redemption amount, so ask before you list or sign a contract.

You can contest what your house is valued at, but not the tax bill itself. Lakewood's cutoff is April 1 of the year at issue, and the petition counts only once it lands at the Ocean County Board of Taxation. Mail it or drop it off early, because the township has no authority to take a petition meant for the county.

A postcard from the assessor arrives on or before February 1 with land, building and total value plus last year's tax. Know the limits before you file:

  • You cannot appeal the land figure and the building figure separately.
  • The assessments on neighboring houses will not serve as your evidence.
  • Pay the first quarter's taxes and municipal charges first, or the appeal cannot be completed.
  • Leaving out a certificate of occupancy does not get you out of an assessment.

You can sit down with the assessor's office by appointment to go over a value before filing anything. The owner carries the burden of proof, so attach three to five comparable sales. If the county board rules against you, the Tax Court takes an appeal within 45 days.

Eligible owners can draw on state programs, while the township assessor's office runs the local deductions. Those are the senior citizen, disability, surviving spouse and veteran deductions, plus the exemption for a disabled veteran. Forms sit in the township's download center.

The fiscal year 2027 state budget pays for Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ. Each has a yearly application window, so look at the Division of Taxation relief page for the next one. Ignore links in unsolicited texts or emails about relief benefits, which the state flags as a scam risk.

A sale can change eligibility, so a seller who receives a benefit should ask the state program office how a mid-year move affects the claim.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell a Lakewood house
sections.html:
Take the tax steps in sequence. Start by asking the assessor who the owner of record is. Next, get the collector's quarter-by-quarter balance, plus word on any lien certificate against the parcel. Think your value is too high? The April 1 cutoff applies, and the petition goes to Toms River rather than the township. Just before closing, order a fresh written payoff, because interest moves the figure daily.

Landlords should pull together leases and rent records. If you inherited the property, bring the papers showing you now own it. No lender is involved in a cash purchase, yet the closing agent still pays the tax and any lien before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the Lakewood property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year being appealed, and the petition must be received by the Ocean County Board of Taxation in Toms River. A petition handed to the township does not count.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lakewood house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Your closing agent requests a payoff from the Lakewood tax collector and pays the balance from your sale proceeds. If a tax sale certificate already exists on the parcel, the lien must be redeemed in full with guaranteed funds before clear title can pass.

faqs.q: How much interest does Lakewood charge on late taxes?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 8% a year on the first $1,500 of delinquency and 18% on the amount above that. A 6% year-end penalty applies when open tax and interest on December 31 exceed $10,000.

faqs.q: Which Lakewood office explains my assessed value?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Assessor at 732-364-2500, extension 5248, in the Municipal Building at 231 Third Street. The office reviews values by appointment on weekdays between 8:30 AM and 5 PM.

faqs.q: Why is my Lakewood second-half tax bill different from the first half?
faqs.a: The first two quarters are set at half of last year's bill, while the last two reflect the rate struck for the current year. If the budgets of the county, school district and township rose, the second half grows, and if they fell it shrinks.
